name: Modern SEO M2 L4: Putting it All Together
body:
> Module 2, 4:18. Source: Lesson 4 Putting it All Together.mp4

## In short
- The three steps (GBP audit, landing page audit, citations) can be implemented for any local business within one to two weeks.
- Results are slower: expect rank map movement within a couple of weeks, and progress that is not linear.
- The target is a rank map with 20 to 40% top three (green) coverage, usually within one to two months in low to medium competition markets.
- If you are stuck at 10 to 15% green after two months, the market is too competitive for this method. Move to Core 30 (Module 3).
- Track the rank map every one to two weeks, document every change with its date, and do not jump to random tactics.

## Key ideas
- **Implementation timeline.** GBP audit and optimization in one session. Landing page audit and fixes the same or next day. LeadSnap setup about 10 minutes, then it runs automatically. The work is not time-consuming; it is about making the right changes systematically. (0:04 to 0:39)
- **Results timeline.** Local SEO is not like paid ads. Movement should start within a couple of weeks, faster if you also join the local chamber of commerce, run the instructor's local SEO offsite analysis prompt, and sponsor local charities. (0:39 to 1:10)
- **Progress is uneven.** Example given: improvement in week three, nothing for two weeks, then big movement in week five. (1:10)
- **The key metric** is rank map top three green coverage of 20 to 40%. (1:10)
- **When to move to Core 30.** The rank map tells you. Steady green progress to 30, 40 or 50% means the basic method is enough. Stuck at 10 to 15% after two months means you need Core 30, which builds topical relevance with pages for every GBP category and service. (1:49)
- **It is not a failure.** You still built the foundation: optimized GBP, aligned landing page, verified citations. Core 30 layers on top. (2:22)
- **Top three is what counts.** "Fourth position or lower is basically invisible." Calls increase as top three coverage spreads. (2:22 to 2:54)
- **Patience and discipline.** Build legitimate signals, track every one to two weeks (not more often), document changes, stick to the system, and do not try everything at once. (2:54 to 3:25)

## Step-by-step process
1. Do the GBP audit and optimization in one session (Lesson 1). (0:04)
2. Do the landing page audit and fixes the same or next day (Lesson 2). (0:04)
3. Set up citations (about 10 minutes in LeadSnap, Lesson 3). (0:04)
4. Optionally add offsite signals: join the local chamber of commerce, run the local SEO offsite analysis prompt, sponsor local charities. (0:39)
5. Track the rank map every one to two weeks. (2:54)
6. Write down each change and the date it was made. (3:25)
7. After about two months, judge the result: 20 to 40% (or more) top three green coverage means the method is working; stuck at 10 to 15% means move to Core 30 (Module 3). (1:10 to 1:49)

## Checklist
- All three steps implemented within one to two weeks
- Offsite extras considered (chamber of commerce, offsite analysis prompt, local charity sponsorship)
- Rank map checked every one to two weeks, not more often
- Change log kept with dates
- No random new tactics added just because results are slow
- Two-month check: top three green coverage compared against the 20 to 40% target
- Decision made: stay with the three steps or move to Core 30

## Tools and resources mentioned
| Tool or resource | What it is used for | Timestamp |
|---|---|---|
| LeadSnap | Citation setup, about 10 minutes | 0:04 |
| Rank map | The key progress metric (top three green coverage) | 1:10, 2:54 |
| Local chamber of commerce | Extra offsite signal that can speed up movement | 0:39 |
| Local SEO offsite analysis prompt (instructor's) | Extra offsite step | 0:39 |
| Local charity sponsorships | Extra offsite signal | 0:39 |
| Core 30 system (Module 3) | Next step for competitive markets | 1:49 |

## Numbers and benchmarks
All are instructor claims, not verified facts.
- Full three-step implementation: within one to two weeks. (0:04)
- LeadSnap setup: about 10 minutes. (0:04)
- First rank map movement: within a couple of weeks. (0:39)
- Target: 20 to 40% top three green coverage, usually within a month or two in low to medium competition markets. (1:10)
- Good progress: steady green growth to 30, 40 or 50% coverage. (1:49)
- Warning sign: stuck at 10 to 15% green after two months. (1:49)
- The three-step method is enough for 70 to 80% of the businesses he works with. (2:22)
- Fourth position or lower is "basically invisible." (2:22)
- Track the rank map every one to two weeks. (2:54)

## Terms
**Green coverage:** The share of rank map grid points where the business ranks in the top three.
**Core 30:** The instructor's advanced system (Module 3) for competitive markets. Builds topical relevance by creating pages for every GBP category and service.
**Low competition ranking method:** The three-step method from Module 1 Lesson 5 (GBP audit, landing page audit, verified citations).

## Worth quoting
- "Fourth position or lower is basically invisible." (2:22)
- "Your rank map will tell you." (1:49)
- "Don't start adding random tactics if you don't see results in a day or two. Stick to the system." (3:25)

## How to use this at TAG
- **Set a baseline and a review date per client.** For Pipeliners, Alphalete and Summit AZ, record the current top three coverage, then check every one to two weeks. Kim's visibility tracker (memory file `project_visibility_tracker.md`) could hold these readings.
- **Keep a dated change log.** Log every GBP, landing page and citation change with its date so rank map changes can be linked to what was done.
- **Use the two-month test.** If a client stays around 10 to 15% top three coverage two months after the three steps, flag it to Kim as a candidate for the Core 30 approach in Module 3.
- **Consider the offsite extras.** Chamber of commerce membership and local charity sponsorship are ideas to raise with Kim and Scott for each client. They may cost money, so they need approval.
- **Set client expectations.** Use the lesson's framing: implementation is quick, results take weeks, progress is uneven.

## Open questions
- Speech says track "every one to two weeks"; the slide says "every two weeks." (2:54, 3:25 frame)
- Speech says don't add tactics "if you don't see results in a day or two"; the slide says "if you don't see immediate results." (3:25)
- Speech says "20 to 40% top three green coverage"; the slide says "20-40% green coverage." (1:10)
- "Stuck at 10 to 15 green" (1:49) is assumed to mean 10 to 15% coverage.
- The "Implementation timeline" slide is numbered 1. No slide numbered 2 was captured in the frames (frames are about 20 seconds apart), so it is unclear whether a numbered "Results timeline" slide existed.
- The "local SEO offsite analysis prompt" is mentioned but not shown or explained in this module.
- Whisper wrote "GVP" (1:49, 2:22). It means GBP.
- No low-confidence lines in the manifest.

## Timestamps
- 0:04 Implementation timeline
- 0:39 Results timeline and offsite extras
- 1:10 Non-linear progress, the 20 to 40% target
- 1:49 When you need Core 30
- 2:22 Not a failure; 70 to 80% of businesses; top three matters
- 2:54 Patience, track every one to two weeks
- 3:25 Document changes, stick to the system, Module 3 preview
- 3:56 Module 4 preview, master this first
